questions.prompt: In a school announcement, what is the main purpose of listening for the key message?
options: To understand the most important information
To count every word the speaker says
To copy the speaker's accent
To interrupt with questions immediately
questions.correctAnswer: To understand the most important information
questions.explanation: The key message tells the listener what the announcement is mainly about and what action may be needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the main message in short oral texts and announcements.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour shows active listening during a group discussion?
options: Facing the speaker and asking a relevant question
Talking to a friend while others speak
Leaving before the speaker finishes
Repeating unrelated jokes loudly
questions.correctAnswer: Facing the speaker and asking a relevant question
questions.explanation: Active listening uses attention, respectful body language, and relevant responses to show understanding.
questions.learningOutcome: Use attentive verbal and non-verbal cues during oral communication.

questions.prompt: A speaker says, 'Our class garden has finally produced vegetables!' with a bright voice. What mood is most likely shown?
options: Excitement
Fear
Boredom
Regret
questions.correctAnswer: Excitement
questions.explanation: A bright voice and the word 'finally' suggest joy and satisfaction about the result.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer mood from a speaker's tone, words, and context.

questions.prompt: What should a learner do before contributing to a formal class discussion?
options: Wait for a turn and speak on the topic
Shout over the current speaker
Change the topic without warning
Mock classmates who disagree
questions.correctAnswer: Wait for a turn and speak on the topic
questions.explanation: Formal discussion requires turn-taking, respect, and relevant contributions.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply turn-taking and topic control in group discussions.

questions.prompt: Which interview question would give the richest answer from a school librarian?
options: How do reading clubs help Grade 8 learners improve?
Is the library open?
Do you have shelves?
Are there books?
questions.correctAnswer: How do reading clubs help Grade 8 learners improve?
questions.explanation: Open-ended questions encourage detailed responses and explanations.
questions.learningOutcome: Ask open-ended questions to obtain useful information in interviews.

questions.prompt: Which word has three syllables?
options: Library
Desk
Chair
Gate
questions.correctAnswer: Library
questions.explanation: Library is commonly pronounced in three syllables: li-bra-ry.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize syllable patterns in common school vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would usually end with rising intonation in speech?
options: Are you joining the debate club today?
The debate club meets today.
We joined the debate club yesterday.
The debate club was busy.
questions.correctAnswer: Are you joining the debate club today?
questions.explanation: Yes-or-no questions often use rising intonation at the end.
questions.learningOutcome: Use intonation patterns to distinguish questions from statements.

questions.prompt: A speaker gives three reasons for keeping the school compound clean. What should a good oral summary include?
options: The three main reasons in brief form
Every pause the speaker made
Only the speaker's first word
A different topic about sports
questions.correctAnswer: The three main reasons in brief form
questions.explanation: A summary keeps the main ideas and leaves out minor details.
questions.learningOutcome: Summarize key points from spoken presentations accurately.

questions.prompt: Which feature is common in an oral narrative?
options: A storyteller and an audience
A chemical formula only
A shopping receipt only
A silent written exam
questions.correctAnswer: A storyteller and an audience
questions.explanation: Oral narratives are performed for listeners and often involve voice, gesture, and audience response.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify features of oral narratives in Kenyan and other contexts.

questions.prompt: In oral communication, why should a speaker vary volume and pace?
options: To keep listeners interested and emphasize important ideas
To confuse the audience deliberately
To avoid preparing the message
To make every word sound the same
questions.correctAnswer: To keep listeners interested and emphasize important ideas
questions.explanation: Variation in voice helps listeners follow meaning and notice key points.
questions.learningOutcome: Use voice control to communicate clearly to an audience.

questions.prompt: During a debate, a learner says, 'I understand your point, but the evidence from our survey shows a different result.' What skill is being used?
options: Respectful rebuttal
Topic avoidance
Name-calling
Silent reading
questions.correctAnswer: Respectful rebuttal
questions.explanation: A rebuttal responds to another argument, and respectful language keeps the discussion fair.
questions.learningOutcome: Use evidence and respectful language when responding to opposing views.

questions.prompt: A presenter looks down, speaks softly, and avoids the audience. Which improvement would help most?
options: Maintain eye contact and project the voice
Read faster without pausing
Hide behind the chart
Use unrelated slang throughout
questions.correctAnswer: Maintain eye contact and project the voice
questions.explanation: Eye contact and clear voice projection help the audience hear and connect with the message.
questions.learningOutcome: Improve oral presentations using effective voice and body language.

questions.prompt: Which preparation is most useful before giving an oral report on a class project?
options: Arrange points in a clear order and practise aloud
Memorise unrelated jokes
Ignore the audience's needs
Carry blank papers only
questions.correctAnswer: Arrange points in a clear order and practise aloud
questions.explanation: Planning and practice make an oral report organised and easier to understand.
questions.learningOutcome: Prepare organized oral reports from class activities and projects.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to persuade classmates to plant trees. Which evidence would strengthen the speech?
options: Local examples of how trees reduce heat and soil erosion
A list of random football scores
A joke about school uniforms
A statement that evidence is unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: Local examples of how trees reduce heat and soil erosion
questions.explanation: Relevant evidence makes a persuasive speech more convincing and practical.
questions.learningOutcome: Support persuasive oral messages with relevant examples and evidence.

questions.prompt: A group discussion becomes heated because two learners disagree about the best project idea. What should the chairperson do first?
options: Remind members of discussion rules and allow each side to speak briefly
End the discussion and choose a favourite idea secretly
Tell the louder learner to decide everything
Mock both ideas so nobody contributes
questions.correctAnswer: Remind members of discussion rules and allow each side to speak briefly
questions.explanation: A chairperson manages order, fairness, and focus so the group can compare ideas respectfully.
questions.learningOutcome: Manage disagreements in discussions using fair procedures.

questions.prompt: A speaker says, 'Well, that was a brilliant idea,' after a plan fails. What should a listener consider before deciding the meaning?
options: Tone and context may show sarcasm
Every positive word is always literal
The statement has no meaning
The listener should ignore the situation
questions.correctAnswer: Tone and context may show sarcasm
questions.explanation: Meaning in speech can depend on tone, situation, and intention, not only dictionary meanings.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer implied meaning from tone, context, and word choice.

questions.prompt: A teacher says, 'First collect data, next arrange it in a table, then present your findings.' What listening skill is needed?
options: Following sequence
Guessing randomly
Ignoring connectors
Changing the task
questions.correctAnswer: Following sequence
questions.explanation: Words such as first, next, and then show the order in which steps should be done.
questions.learningOutcome: Follow ordered oral instructions using sequence markers.

questions.prompt: A Grade 8 learner will speak to parents, teachers, and learners at an education day. Which choice best adapts to the audience?
options: Use respectful standard English and examples familiar to the whole school community
Use private slang that only close friends understand
Speak as if only the head teacher is present
Use technical terms without explaining them
questions.correctAnswer: Use respectful standard English and examples familiar to the whole school community
questions.explanation: Audience awareness helps a speaker choose language, tone, and examples that suit listeners.
questions.learningOutcome: Adapt oral language to audience, purpose, and situation.

questions.prompt: A class hears a rumour about exam dates from an unknown speaker outside school. What is the best response?
options: Verify the information with an official school source
Spread the rumour quickly
Stop attending lessons immediately
Assume every rumour is accurate
questions.correctAnswer: Verify the information with an official school source
questions.explanation: Listeners should check important information with reliable sources before acting on it.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate reliability of spoken information before sharing or using it.

questions.prompt: Which opening would best begin a formal speech about improving reading culture in school?
options: Good morning teachers and fellow learners; today I will share practical ways to make reading part of our daily school life.
Hey people, books are everywhere, so let me just talk.
I do not know why I am here, but reading exists.
This speech has no topic and no plan.
questions.correctAnswer: Good morning teachers and fellow learners; today I will share practical ways to make reading part of our daily school life.
questions.explanation: A strong formal opening greets the audience, names the topic, and signals a clear purpose.
questions.learningOutcome: Create appropriate openings for formal speeches on school and community issues.

questions.prompt: What is skimming used for when reading a passage?
options: Getting the general idea quickly
Finding one exact date only
Copying every sentence
Checking handwriting style
questions.correctAnswer: Getting the general idea quickly
questions.explanation: Skimming is a fast reading strategy used to grasp the main idea of a text.
questions.learningOutcome: Use skimming to identify the general idea of a text.

questions.prompt: What is scanning used for when reading?
options: Finding specific information quickly
Reading aloud for drama
Changing the author's words
Guessing without looking at the text
questions.correctAnswer: Finding specific information quickly
questions.explanation: Scanning helps a reader locate a name, number, date, or other precise detail.
questions.learningOutcome: Use scanning to locate specific details in texts.

questions.prompt: In the sentence, 'The drought made water scarce, so the school stored every drop,' what does scarce mean?
options: Not enough
Very colourful
Easy to waste
Noisy
questions.correctAnswer: Not enough
questions.explanation: The clue 'stored every drop' shows that water was limited.
questions.learningOutcome: Use surrounding words to infer meanings of unfamiliar vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the main idea of a paragraph?
options: The most important point the paragraph develops
The last punctuation mark in the paragraph
The longest word in the paragraph
The writer's handwriting pattern
questions.correctAnswer: The most important point the paragraph develops
questions.explanation: The main idea is the central thought that the details support.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify main ideas and supporting details in paragraphs.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is an opinion?
options: The new school library is the best building in town.
The library opened on Monday.
The library has four reading tables.
The library closes at five o'clock.
questions.correctAnswer: The new school library is the best building in town.
questions.explanation: An opinion expresses a personal judgement that may differ from one reader to another.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish facts from opinions in informational texts.

questions.prompt: In the sentence, 'Because the road flooded, the bus arrived late,' what is the cause?
options: The road flooded
The bus arrived late
The bus was yellow
The learners were seated
questions.correctAnswer: The road flooded
questions.explanation: The cause is the event that leads to the result, and here flooding led to lateness.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify cause and effect relationships in sentences and paragraphs.

questions.prompt: A story says, 'Achieng packed her umbrella after seeing dark clouds.' What can the reader infer?
options: She expected rain
She planned to swim
She disliked umbrellas
She had finished lunch
questions.correctAnswer: She expected rain
questions.explanation: Dark clouds and carrying an umbrella suggest that Achieng thought it might rain.
questions.learningOutcome: Make reasonable inferences from textual clues.

questions.prompt: A text explains how to prepare a kitchen garden step by step. What is the author's main purpose?
options: To instruct
To entertain with jokes
To complain without evidence
To hide information
questions.correctAnswer: To instruct
questions.explanation: Step-by-step information usually aims to guide readers through a process.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine an author's purpose from text structure and content.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would best support the topic sentence, 'Exercise improves learning'?
options: Physical activity can increase concentration during lessons.
The classroom wall is painted blue.
A desk has four legs.
The market opens early on Saturdays.
questions.correctAnswer: Physical activity can increase concentration during lessons.
questions.explanation: A supporting detail should explain or give evidence for the topic sentence.
questions.learningOutcome: Match supporting details to main ideas in paragraphs.

questions.prompt: In the sentence, 'The learners cleaned the hall because they wanted it ready for visitors,' what does 'it' refer to?
options: The hall
The learners
The visitors
The cleaning
questions.correctAnswer: The hall
questions.explanation: The pronoun 'it' replaces the noun 'hall' in the sentence.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify pronoun references to improve reading comprehension.

questions.prompt: Which connector best shows contrast in a paragraph?
options: However
Therefore
First
Similarly
questions.correctAnswer: However
questions.explanation: However signals that the next idea differs from or opposes the previous one.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret connectors that show contrast, sequence, and cause.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is the best summary of a passage about conserving water at school?
options: Learners can conserve water by fixing leaks, closing taps, and reusing safe water for gardens.
A tap is made of metal and can shine.
Some learners carry blue bottles to school.
The passage has six paragraphs and several commas.
questions.correctAnswer: Learners can conserve water by fixing leaks, closing taps, and reusing safe water for gardens.
questions.explanation: A good summary combines the central ideas without unnecessary details.
questions.learningOutcome: Write concise summaries that preserve main ideas.

questions.prompt: In the line, 'The classroom buzzed like a busy market,' what is being compared?
options: The classroom noise and a busy market
The desks and vegetables
The teacher and a trader
The books and coins
questions.correctAnswer: The classroom noise and a busy market
questions.explanation: The simile uses 'like' to compare the classroom's noise to the sound of a market.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret similes and other figurative expressions in context.

questions.prompt: A learner finds two articles about climate change, one from a science organisation and one from an unknown blog with no author. Which article is more reliable?
options: The science organisation article with named evidence
The unknown blog because it has no author
The shorter article automatically
The article with the largest font
questions.correctAnswer: The science organisation article with named evidence
questions.explanation: Reliable sources usually identify authors or organisations and support claims with evidence.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate credibility of print and digital information sources.

questions.prompt: A story follows a learner who keeps practising after losing a race and later improves. Which theme best fits the story?
options: Perseverance
Wastefulness
Dishonesty
Carelessness
questions.correctAnswer: Perseverance
questions.explanation: The repeated effort after failure points to the theme of perseverance.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze events to identify themes in short prose texts.

questions.prompt: A chapter ends with a character hiding a letter before visitors arrive. What prediction is most reasonable?
options: The letter may become important later in the story
The story has no conflict left
The visitors will never appear
The character cannot read any words
questions.correctAnswer: The letter may become important later in the story
questions.explanation: A hidden letter creates suspense and suggests future consequences.
questions.learningOutcome: Use textual clues to make and justify predictions.

questions.prompt: Which statement shows bias in a text about school clubs?
options: Only members of the drama club are talented; all other clubs are useless.
The drama club meets on Tuesday.
The science club has twenty members.
The chess club uses the library.
questions.correctAnswer: Only members of the drama club are talented; all other clubs are useless.
questions.explanation: Bias shows unfair preference or judgement instead of balanced information.
questions.learningOutcome: Detect biased language and unsupported generalizations in texts.

questions.prompt: A notice says, 'Debate practice: Wednesday, 3:30 p.m., Room 8, topic: digital safety.' Which detail tells where the practice will happen?
options: Room 8
Wednesday
Digital safety
questions.correctAnswer: Room 8
questions.explanation: The location detail in the notice is Room 8.
questions.learningOutcome: Extract specific information from notices, timetables, and announcements.

questions.prompt: Which pair of sentences is most coherent?
options: The learners collected plastic bottles. Then they sorted them for recycling.
The learners collected bottles. The moon tasted loud.
The bell rang. Therefore, mangoes became invisible.
The library opened. However, two plus two is four.
questions.correctAnswer: The learners collected plastic bottles. Then they sorted them for recycling.
questions.explanation: Coherent sentences connect logically and guide the reader from one idea to the next.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze logical flow between sentences in a text.

questions.prompt: Which reading plan is strongest for researching whether school gardens improve nutrition?
options: Read several credible sources, note main claims, compare evidence, and record source details.
Read one anonymous post and copy it without checking.
Use only the first sentence of any article.
Avoid taking notes and rely on memory only.
questions.correctAnswer: Read several credible sources, note main claims, compare evidence, and record source details.
questions.explanation: Good research reading uses credible sources, evidence comparison, and organized notes.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a reading plan for gathering and evaluating information from multiple sources.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the simple past tense?
options: The learners visited the museum.
The learners visit the museum.
The learners will visit the museum.
The learners are visiting the museum.
questions.correctAnswer: The learners visited the museum.
questions.explanation: Visited shows that the action happened in the past.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify simple past tense forms in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?
options: The teacher explains the task clearly.
The teacher explain the task clearly.
The teacher explaining the task clearly.
The teacher have explained the task clearly.
questions.correctAnswer: The teacher explains the task clearly.
questions.explanation: A singular subject in the simple present usually takes a verb ending in -s or -es.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize correct agreement between subjects and verbs.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a comma correctly?
options: After lunch, we cleaned the classroom.
After, lunch we cleaned the classroom.
After lunch we, cleaned the classroom.
After lunch we cleaned, the classroom.
questions.correctAnswer: After lunch, we cleaned the classroom.
questions.explanation: A comma can separate an introductory phrase from the main clause.
questions.learningOutcome: Use commas after introductory words and phrases.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence: 'The books are on the table, but the pen is ___ the drawer'?
options: in
quickly
because
happy
questions.correctAnswer: in
questions.explanation: The preposition 'in' shows location inside the drawer.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose appropriate prepositions to show place and position.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a modal verb to show obligation?
options: Learners must return library books on time.
Learners returned books yesterday.
Learners are reading books.
Learners like storybooks.
questions.correctAnswer: Learners must return library books on time.
questions.explanation: Must is a modal verb that can express obligation or necessity.
questions.learningOutcome: Use modal verbs to express obligation, ability, and possibility.

questions.prompt: Which conjunction best joins the sentence: 'We wanted to play outside, ___ it started raining'?
options: but
under
very
near
questions.correctAnswer: but
questions.explanation: But joins contrasting ideas: wanting to play and rain preventing it.
questions.learningOutcome: Use conjunctions to connect related and contrasting ideas.

questions.prompt: Which word is an adverb in the sentence, 'Musa answered the question confidently'?
options: confidently
Musa
question
answered
questions.correctAnswer: confidently
questions.explanation: Confidently describes how Musa answered, so it functions as an adverb.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify adverbs that describe manner in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence changes 'The prefect opened the gate' into passive voice?
options: The gate was opened by the prefect.
The prefect was opening the gate.
The gate opened the prefect.
The prefect opens the gate.
questions.correctAnswer: The gate was opened by the prefect.
questions.explanation: The passive voice makes the object of the active sentence the subject of the new sentence.
questions.learningOutcome: Transform simple active sentences into passive voice.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a relative pronoun correctly?
options: The learner who won the race thanked her coach.
The learner what won the race thanked her coach.
The learner because won the race thanked her coach.
The learner quickly won who thanked her coach.
questions.correctAnswer: The learner who won the race thanked her coach.
questions.explanation: Who introduces a relative clause that gives more information about the learner.
questions.learningOutcome: Use relative pronouns to add information about people and things.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly reports, 'I am preparing for the quiz,' said Njeri?
options: Njeri said that she was preparing for the quiz.
Njeri said that I am preparing for the quiz.
Njeri said that she is prepare for the quiz.
Njeri said preparing quiz.
questions.correctAnswer: Njeri said that she was preparing for the quiz.
questions.explanation: Reported speech changes the pronoun and often shifts the tense back.
questions.learningOutcome: Convert direct speech into reported speech with appropriate pronouns and tense.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the first conditional correctly?
options: If it rains, we will move the meeting indoors.
If it rains, we moved the meeting indoors yesterday.
If it will rain, we move yesterday.
If rain, meeting indoors.
questions.correctAnswer: If it rains, we will move the meeting indoors.
questions.explanation: The first conditional uses present simple after if and will for a likely future result.
questions.learningOutcome: Use first conditional sentences to express possible future results.

questions.prompt: Which option best completes the sentence: 'Either the captain or the players ___ responsible for arranging the balls'?
options: are
is
was
has
questions.correctAnswer: are
questions.explanation: With either...or, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, and players is plural.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply agreement rules with compound subjects joined by either...or.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a question tag properly?
options: You completed the assignment, didn't you?
You completed the assignment, did you?
You completed the assignment, do you?
You completed the assignment, aren't it?
questions.correctAnswer: You completed the assignment, didn't you?
questions.explanation: A positive statement usually takes a negative question tag with the matching auxiliary.
questions.learningOutcome: Use question tags that match tense and polarity.

questions.prompt: Which sentence avoids a dangling modifier?
options: While walking to school, I saw a rainbow over the hills.
While walking to school, a rainbow appeared over the hills.
Walking to school, the hills saw a rainbow.
While walking to school, the classroom was painted.
questions.correctAnswer: While walking to school, I saw a rainbow over the hills.
questions.explanation: The sentence clearly shows that I was walking to school, so the modifier has a logical subject.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze sentences to correct misplaced or dangling modifiers.

questions.prompt: Which sentence keeps parallel structure?
options: The club teaches reading, writing, and speaking.
The club teaches reading, to write, and speeches.
The club teaches to read, writing, and speak.
The club teaches readers, writing, and to speak.
questions.correctAnswer: The club teaches reading, writing, and speaking.
questions.explanation: Parallel structure uses the same grammatical pattern for items in a list.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise sentences so listed ideas follow a consistent grammatical pattern.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the homophone 'their' correctly?
options: The learners carried their books to the library.
The learners carried there books to the library.
The learners carried they're books to the library.
The learners carried they are books to the library.
questions.correctAnswer: The learners carried their books to the library.
questions.explanation: Their shows possession, while there refers to place and they're means they are.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose accurate homophones according to meaning and context.

questions.prompt: Which sentence combines the ideas most effectively: 'The road was muddy. We arrived on time'?
options: Although the road was muddy, we arrived on time.
The road was muddy because we arrived on time.
We arrived on time unless the road was muddy.
The road was muddy, or we arrived on time.
questions.correctAnswer: Although the road was muddy, we arrived on time.
questions.explanation: Although shows contrast between the difficult road condition and the successful arrival.
questions.learningOutcome: Combine related ideas using subordinating conjunctions accurately.

questions.prompt: Which revision best improves this sentence: 'The committee meet yesterday and decides the trip will started early'?
options: The committee met yesterday and decided the trip would start early.
The committee meet yesterday and decide the trip starts early.
The committee meeting yesterday and decided trip started.
The committee met yesterday and decides the trip will started early.
questions.correctAnswer: The committee met yesterday and decided the trip would start early.
questions.explanation: The revision keeps past tense forms consistent and uses a correct verb phrase for the planned action.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise sentences for tense consistency and grammatical accuracy.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best combines cause, contrast, and result in a clear way?
options: Although the team had little time because the bus was late, they presented confidently.
Because although the team little time bus late presented.
The bus was late although because confidently.
The team confidently bus late little time although.
questions.correctAnswer: Although the team had little time because the bus was late, they presented confidently.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses subordinate clauses clearly while keeping the main idea easy to follow.
questions.learningOutcome: Create clear complex sentences that show relationships among ideas.

questions.prompt: Which version is the strongest formal sentence for a report?
options: The survey indicates that most Grade 8 learners prefer reading after lunch.
Most kids kinda like reading later, you know.
Reading after lunch is cool and stuff.
Grade 8 people just vibe with books after eating.
questions.correctAnswer: The survey indicates that most Grade 8 learners prefer reading after lunch.
questions.explanation: Formal writing uses precise vocabulary and avoids slang or vague expressions.
questions.learningOutcome: Select language register appropriate for formal school reports.

questions.prompt: What is a topic sentence in a paragraph?
options: A sentence that states the main idea of the paragraph
A sentence that must always be a question
A sentence copied from the title only
A sentence with no connection to the paragraph
questions.correctAnswer: A sentence that states the main idea of the paragraph
questions.explanation: A topic sentence introduces or states the main idea that the paragraph develops.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify and write effective topic sentences for paragraphs.

questions.prompt: Which part of a friendly letter usually comes after the writer's address and date?
options: Greeting
Signature of the head teacher
Index
Bibliography
questions.correctAnswer: Greeting
questions.explanation: A friendly letter commonly includes address, date, greeting, body, closing, and name.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize the main parts of informal letters.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would best begin a narrative about a surprising event at school?
options: The bell had just rung when a strange sound came from the science room.
This composition will talk about many things.
School is a place with buildings.
I am writing because writing is required.
questions.correctAnswer: The bell had just rung when a strange sound came from the science room.
questions.explanation: A strong narrative opening creates interest and introduces a situation.
questions.learningOutcome: Write engaging openings for narratives based on familiar experiences.

questions.prompt: Which detail is most useful in descriptive writing about a market?
options: The smell of ripe mangoes and the calls of traders
The fact that markets are places
The word market repeated many times
A list of unrelated phone numbers
questions.correctAnswer: The smell of ripe mangoes and the calls of traders
questions.explanation: Descriptive writing uses sensory details to help the reader imagine the scene.
questions.learningOutcome: Use sensory details to describe people, places, and events vividly.

questions.prompt: Which closing is most suitable for a formal letter to the principal?
options: Yours faithfully,
Cheers,
See you soon,
Your classmate,
questions.correctAnswer: Yours faithfully,
questions.explanation: Formal letters use respectful closings such as Yours faithfully or Yours sincerely.
questions.learningOutcome: Use appropriate format and tone in formal letters.

questions.prompt: Which subject line is clearest for an email requesting permission to visit a museum?
options: Request for Permission to Visit the Museum
Hi
Very Important Things
Something About Somewhere
questions.correctAnswer: Request for Permission to Visit the Museum
questions.explanation: A clear subject line states the purpose of the email directly.
questions.learningOutcome: Write clear subject lines and messages for formal emails.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would be most appropriate in the minutes of a class meeting?
options: The class agreed to clean the compound every Friday.
We had a super funny time and laughed loudly.
Some people said things that I forgot.
The meeting was boring and too long.
questions.correctAnswer: The class agreed to clean the compound every Friday.
questions.explanation: Minutes record decisions and important points in a clear, objective way.
questions.learningOutcome: Record meeting decisions accurately using suitable language.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best supports the topic sentence, 'Reading improves vocabulary'?
options: When learners meet new words in stories, they can learn meanings from context.
The football field is behind the dining hall.
A ruler is useful in geometry.
Some doors are made of metal.
questions.correctAnswer: When learners meet new words in stories, they can learn meanings from context.
questions.explanation: A supporting sentence should explain or give evidence for the topic sentence.
questions.learningOutcome: Develop paragraphs using relevant supporting details.

questions.prompt: Which transition best completes the sentence: 'The class revised carefully; ___, many learners improved their scores'?
options: therefore
however
before
instead
questions.correctAnswer: therefore
questions.explanation: Therefore shows a result of the careful revision.
questions.learningOutcome: Use transition words to connect ideas logically in writing.

questions.prompt: Which thesis statement is strongest for an essay on school gardens?
options: School gardens should be supported because they teach responsibility, improve nutrition, and make good use of space.
Gardens are there and some people like them.
This essay is about gardens in general.
A garden has plants.
questions.correctAnswer: School gardens should be supported because they teach responsibility, improve nutrition, and make good use of space.
questions.explanation: A strong thesis states a clear position and previews the main supporting points.
questions.learningOutcome: Write clear thesis statements for opinion and argumentative essays.

questions.prompt: Which line of dialogue is punctuated correctly?
options: "Please close the window," said Baraka.
"Please close the window" said Baraka.
"Please close the window, said Baraka."
Please close the window," said Baraka.
questions.correctAnswer: "Please close the window," said Baraka.
questions.explanation: Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks, and the comma comes before the closing quotation mark.
questions.learningOutcome: Punctuate direct speech accurately in written dialogue.

questions.prompt: Which note is most suitable for a notice board?
options: Environmental Club members will meet in Room 4 on Friday at 3:20 p.m.
I think maybe people should know something soon.
Everyone should guess where the meeting is.
The club is clubbing about club things.
questions.correctAnswer: Environmental Club members will meet in Room 4 on Friday at 3:20 p.m.
questions.explanation: A notice should give clear information about who, what, where, and when.
questions.learningOutcome: Write clear notices for school events and activities.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would fit best in a diary entry?
options: Today I felt proud when our group presented the science project successfully.
The meeting was called to order at exactly 2:00 p.m.
Dear Sir, I request permission to leave early.
The agenda contained three official items.
questions.correctAnswer: Today I felt proud when our group presented the science project successfully.
questions.explanation: A diary entry often records personal experiences, feelings, and reflections.
questions.learningOutcome: Write reflective diary entries using personal voice and clear events.

questions.prompt: Which revision makes this sentence more precise: 'The thing was nice and good'?
options: The school mural was colourful and well balanced.
The thing was very thing-like.
The stuff was somehow okay.
The nice good thing was nice.
questions.correctAnswer: The school mural was colourful and well balanced.
questions.explanation: Precise nouns and adjectives give readers clearer information than vague words.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise writing by replacing vague words with precise vocabulary.

questions.prompt: A report about a class survey includes personal jokes and guesses. What revision is most needed?
options: Remove informal jokes and support claims with survey findings
Add more private jokes
Hide the survey results
Write only the title
questions.correctAnswer: Remove informal jokes and support claims with survey findings
questions.explanation: Reports should be objective, clear, and based on evidence from the activity or research.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise reports for objectivity, evidence, and formal tone.

questions.prompt: Which paragraph order is best for an argumentative essay?
options: Introduction with position, supporting reasons, response to opposing view, conclusion
Conclusion, random joke, title, unrelated list
Opposing view only, no position, no conclusion
Title, blank page, signature, greeting
questions.correctAnswer: Introduction with position, supporting reasons, response to opposing view, conclusion
questions.explanation: Argumentative writing needs a clear position, evidence, consideration of other views, and a conclusion.
questions.learningOutcome: Organize argumentative essays using claims, reasons, counterpoints, and conclusions.

questions.prompt: Which sentence should be removed from a paragraph about benefits of public libraries?
options: Goats need balanced feeding during dry seasons.
Libraries give learners access to many books.
Libraries provide quiet spaces for study.
Library programmes can encourage reading habits.
questions.correctAnswer: Goats need balanced feeding during dry seasons.
questions.explanation: That sentence is unrelated to public libraries and weakens paragraph unity.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise paragraphs by removing irrelevant details.

questions.prompt: Which plan would produce the strongest feature article about a local community project?
options: Interview participants, observe the project, gather facts, draft with a human-interest angle, and edit for accuracy.
Invent all details and avoid checking names.
Write only opinions without examples.
Copy a poster and call it an article.
questions.correctAnswer: Interview participants, observe the project, gather facts, draft with a human-interest angle, and edit for accuracy.
questions.explanation: A feature article is strongest when it combines accurate reporting, vivid detail, and careful editing.
questions.learningOutcome: Create feature articles using interviews, observation, factual detail, and revision.

questions.prompt: Which checklist best supports final editing of an essay?
options: Check structure, grammar, punctuation, spelling, word choice, and relevance to the topic.
Check only the colour of the pen.
Count pages without reading them.
Look at the title and ignore the body.
questions.correctAnswer: Check structure, grammar, punctuation, spelling, word choice, and relevance to the topic.
questions.explanation: Final editing should review both language accuracy and how well the writing answers the task.
questions.learningOutcome: Create and apply editing checklists for polished written work.

questions.prompt: Which ending best concludes a speech encouraging learners to protect school property?
options: Let us protect every desk, book, and tap because shared property supports learning for all of us.
That is all, and I have nothing connected to say.
School property exists somewhere, so goodbye.
I forgot the topic but the speech is over.
questions.correctAnswer: Let us protect every desk, book, and tap because shared property supports learning for all of us.
questions.explanation: An effective conclusion reinforces the message and leaves the audience with a clear call to action.
questions.learningOutcome: Create effective conclusions for speeches with clear calls to action.

questions.prompt: What is the plot of a story?
options: The sequence of events in the story
The colour of the book cover
The number of pages only
The author's handwriting
questions.correctAnswer: The sequence of events in the story
questions.explanation: Plot refers to how events are arranged from beginning to end.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify plot as a basic element of prose narratives.

questions.prompt: Who is a character in a story?
options: A person or figure who takes part in the events
A comma at the end of a sentence
A page number in the book
A list of chapter titles only
questions.correctAnswer: A person or figure who takes part in the events
questions.explanation: Characters are the people or figures whose actions and choices shape the story.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify characters and their roles in literary texts.

questions.prompt: What is setting in literature?
options: The time and place of events
The price of a storybook
The number of commas in a poem
The size of the classroom only
questions.correctAnswer: The time and place of events
questions.explanation: Setting tells where and when events happen in a text.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify setting and explain its role in literary texts.

questions.prompt: What is a theme in a literary text?
options: A central idea or message explored by the text
The page where the story begins
The author's favourite pen
A spelling mistake in dialogue
questions.correctAnswer: A central idea or message explored by the text
questions.explanation: A theme is a deeper idea developed through events, characters, and language.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize theme as a central idea in poems, stories, and plays.

questions.prompt: What is conflict in a story?
options: A struggle or problem that drives the action
The title page of a book
A list of difficult words only
A quiet pause after reading
questions.correctAnswer: A struggle or problem that drives the action
questions.explanation: Conflict creates tension and gives characters something to respond to or solve.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify conflicts that move stories forward.

questions.prompt: Which line contains a simile?
options: Her smile was like morning sunlight.
Her smile was morning sunlight.
The smile walked to town.
The smile had three pages.
questions.correctAnswer: Her smile was like morning sunlight.
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using like or as.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify similes in poems and prose extracts.

questions.prompt: Which line contains personification?
options: The wind whispered through the maize field.
The wind moved through the maize field.
The maize field was green.
The wind came at noon.
questions.correctAnswer: The wind whispered through the maize field.
questions.explanation: Personification gives a human action, whispering, to the wind.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize personification and explain its effect.

questions.prompt: What is a stanza in a poem?
options: A group of lines arranged together
A character's secret plan
The price of a poetry book
A punctuation mark at the end
questions.correctAnswer: A group of lines arranged together
questions.explanation: A stanza is a unit of lines in a poem, similar to a paragraph in prose.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify stanzas and other structural features of poems.

questions.prompt: In a play, what does dialogue reveal most directly?
options: What characters say to each other
The weight of the stage curtains
The printer used for the script
The exact number of seats in the hall
questions.correctAnswer: What characters say to each other
questions.explanation: Dialogue is the spoken exchange between characters and can reveal thoughts, relationships, and conflict.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify dialogue and explain its function in drama.

questions.prompt: What does mood mean in a poem or story?
options: The feeling created for the reader
The number of chapters
The writer's address
The font size used
questions.correctAnswer: The feeling created for the reader
questions.explanation: Mood is the atmosphere or feeling a text creates through language and events.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe mood using clues from language and situation.

questions.prompt: A character shares food with a hungry classmate even though lunch is scarce. Which trait is most clearly shown?
options: Generosity
Selfishness
Cowardice
Carelessness
questions.correctAnswer: Generosity
questions.explanation: Sharing limited food to help someone else shows kindness and generosity.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer character traits from actions and choices in literary texts.

questions.prompt: A story begins in a dry village where families queue for water. How does the setting likely affect the story?
options: It creates a challenge around water scarcity
It proves the story has no problem
It makes every character wealthy
It removes the need for action
questions.correctAnswer: It creates a challenge around water scarcity
questions.explanation: A dry setting with water queues suggests pressure, conflict, and decisions about limited resources.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how setting can shape conflict and character choices.

questions.prompt: In a poem, repeated words at the beginning of several lines are most likely used to create what effect?
options: Emphasis and rhythm
A shopping list
A mathematical answer
A stage direction only
questions.correctAnswer: Emphasis and rhythm
questions.explanation: Repetition can stress an idea and create a memorable sound pattern.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the effect of repetition in poetry.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains the proverb, 'A stitch in time saves nine'?
options: Solving a small problem early prevents a bigger problem later.
Clothes are always more important than books.
Nine stitches are never enough.
Time can be sewn with a needle.
questions.correctAnswer: Solving a small problem early prevents a bigger problem later.
questions.explanation: The proverb teaches the value of acting early before a problem grows.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret proverbs and relate them to everyday situations.

questions.prompt: A poem describes drums, ululations, and colourful clothes at a community celebration. Which sense is mainly appealed to by 'drums'?
options: Hearing
Taste
Smell
Touch
questions.correctAnswer: Hearing
questions.explanation: Drums are associated with sound, so the image appeals mainly to hearing.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sensory images and the senses they appeal to in poetry.

questions.prompt: A narrator says, 'I could not believe what I saw at the river.' Which point of view is being used?
options: First person
Second person
Third person
Omniscient only
questions.correctAnswer: First person
questions.explanation: The pronoun I shows that the narrator is telling the story from a first-person point of view.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify point of view from pronouns and narrative voice.

questions.prompt: A character refuses to apologise after damaging a neighbour's fence, and later loses community trust. What lesson is most supported?
options: Taking responsibility helps maintain relationships.
Damaging property always brings rewards.
Apologies are never useful.
Neighbours should not talk to one another.
questions.correctAnswer: Taking responsibility helps maintain relationships.
questions.explanation: The consequence shows that refusing responsibility can harm trust and relationships.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze events to derive moral lessons from stories.

questions.prompt: A play uses stage directions such as '[She whispers and steps away from the door.]' What do these directions help readers understand?
options: The actor's movement and manner of speaking
The price of the theatre ticket
The exact number of pages
The dictionary meaning of every word
questions.correctAnswer: The actor's movement and manner of speaking
questions.explanation: Stage directions guide performance by showing actions, gestures, tone, and movement.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how stage directions support performance and interpretation.

questions.prompt: Which response best evaluates a character who reports cheating even when friends pressure him to stay silent?
options: He shows integrity because he chooses honesty despite pressure.
He shows laziness because he speaks to a teacher.
He shows greed because he protects fairness.
He shows carelessness because he refuses to hide wrongdoing.
questions.correctAnswer: He shows integrity because he chooses honesty despite pressure.
questions.explanation: Evaluation of character should connect actions with values and consequences in the text.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate characters by linking choices, values, and consequences.

questions.prompt: Which ending would best complete a story about two rivals who learn to work together during a school clean-up?
options: They agree to lead the next clean-up as a team, having discovered that cooperation helps everyone.
They forget the clean-up and never speak again for no reason.
The story changes into a recipe without explanation.
A stranger removes the school and ends the problem instantly.
questions.correctAnswer: They agree to lead the next clean-up as a team, having discovered that cooperation helps everyone.
questions.explanation: A fitting ending resolves the conflict and reinforces the story's theme of cooperation.
questions.learningOutcome: Create plausible story endings that resolve conflict and support theme.

questions.prompt: COMPREHENSION Read the comprehension below and use it to answer questions 1 - 7 The market was noisy and crowded with buyers and sellers. Fruits and vegetables were on the display in stands. Traders waited at their stalls, hoping to sell their goods and make a profit. Tatu walked round the stalls. She admired the fashionable shoes and sweet smelling perfumes on display. The vegetables included round red tomatoes, fresh carrots, huge cabbages and bright crisp spinach. Tatu went to Mutahis stall where he sold fruits and vegetables. She was planning to prepare a special feast for her family. "Good morning my friend." she greeted him. "Good morning Tatu." "How can I help you?" Mutahi enquired. Tatu gave him a long list of items which Mutahi was to pack in her shopping bag. Mutahi then calculated how much she owed. After paying him, Mutahi packed everything she had bought. Tatu carried her packed bag and left the market munching the salty groundnuts which Mutahi had offered her. It was part of customer service. She imagined the smell of the delicious food she would prepare. Learners Score. When she reached home and opened her bag, Tatu found stones inside it. She had been tricked!, "Wooi," "Wooi" She screamed of course, she could not feed her family on stones! Neighbours heard her screams and crowded into her home. On hearing her story, two friends offered to go back to the market with her to look for the trickster. When the arrived, Tatu showed Mutahi the stones in her bag. Her voice was agitated and loud. Some of the vendors hurriedly closed their shops and went to listen to the allegations. Tatu had come to demand for a refund. She was prepared to file a complaint at the police station if her demand was not met. Mutai denied any foul play. He reminded everyone that he had practised integrity for the many years he had served people in Tutamu market. Even so, the merchants were worried it would give their market a bad reputation. Beatrice, who was at the closest stall, was expected to be a witness. However, she had been so busy when Tatu was shopping that she could not recount any details. The mystery puzzled everyone. While they were still wondering what to do. Beatrice invited two vendors to her stall. Unknown to the other vendors she installed a camera at the entrance. When they checked the recording, they saw that after picking the shopping from Mutahi, Tatu had stopped to use her mobile phone. A woman behind her had quickly picked her bag and replaced it with a similar looking bag. Questions: 1. What is the story about?
questions.correctAnswer: 1. The story is about Tatu's experience at the market where she was tricked and ended up with a bag of stones instead of her purchased goods.
questions.explanation: From G8-ENGLISH-2024-TEACHER-CO-KE marking scheme.

questions.prompt: What helped you understand what the story is about?
questions.correctAnswer: The description of Tatu's shopping experience, her discovery of the stones in the bag, and the subsequent confrontation at the market provide a clear narrative of the main events. Additionally, the details about Tatu's interaction with Mutahi and the involvement of neighbors and vendors help contextualize the story.
questions.explanation: From G8-ENGLISH-2024-TEACHER-CO-KE marking scheme.

questions.prompt: What was the reason for Tatu visit to the market?
questions.correctAnswer: Tatu visited the market to buy fruits and vegetables to prepare a special feast for her family.
questions.explanation: From G8-ENGLISH-2024-TEACHER-CO-KE marking scheme.

questions.prompt: Mention two character traits of Mutahi
questions.correctAnswer: -Integrity: Mutahi is described as having practiced integrity for many years at Tutamu market. - Customer-friendly: He demonstrates good customer service by offering Tatu salty groundnuts.
questions.explanation: From G8-ENGLISH-2024-TEACHER-CO-KE marking scheme.

questions.prompt: How did Mutahi react to the allegations?
questions.correctAnswer: Mutahi denied any foul play and reminded everyone of his long- standing integrity in the market. He maintained his innocence throughout the confrontation.
questions.explanation: From G8-ENGLISH-2024-TEACHER-CO-KE marking scheme.

questions.prompt: Provide synonyms for the following words a) Idle b) Last c) Mad d) Naked e) Neat
questions.correctAnswer: a) Inactive b) Final c) Insane d) Bare e) Tidy
questions.explanation: From G8-ENGLISH-2024-TEACHER-CO-KE marking scheme.

questions.prompt: Supply the correct question tags. a) It is going to rain today, b) To make a good home, you need a lot of money c) Maasai people seldom eat fish. d) Let us play, e) He is very regretful now, Write a composition ending with the following words. ......................................................................It was then when I realised that bad company ruins good morals
questions.correctAnswer: a) isn't it? b) don't you? c) do they? d) shall we? e) isn't he? Composition:Teacher to assess.
